metadata.pr_title: Add nodes for basic string operations
metadata.pr_description:
String nodes, requested in RFC https://github.com/Kosinkadink/rfcs/blob/main/rfcs/0000-corenodes.md#string-nodes
Designed nodes:
1. Concatenate, and input is: 
- string_a, 
- string_b 
- separator
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/894c0afc-664f-49a2-a0de-ed60c2aacfc5)
2. Substring, and input is:
- string
- start
- end
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ab814a6-f360-43cb-86be-ac61486c9a78)

3. Length, and input is
- string
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb4f7413-2f59-4faf-aaa7-cc3b0fbf4322)

4. Case Converter, and input is
- string
- mode, with options are ["UPPERCASE", "lowercase", "Capitalize", "Title Case"]
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba1041fd-40f5-4af0-a52b-c0df3ae3d3e4)

5. Trim, and input is
- string
- mode, with options are ["BOTH", "LEFT", "RIGHT"]
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6489d7d8-ab78-4e9e-b172-b4f7e3cbacb2)

6. Replace, and input is
- string
- find
- replace
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/997c09d6-75f2-4e71-90d5-6d0f77cfcb09)

7. Contains, and input is
- string
- substring
- case_sensitive
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e66adb5b-02de-4ba8-b848-f9f83215e694)

8. Compare, and input is
- string_a
- string_b
- mode, with options are ["StartsWith", "EndsWith", "Equal"]
- case_sensitive
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dd3b9ae-f3d8-41bc-90c2-8e459a923840)

9. Regex Match, and input is
- string
- regex_pattern
- case_insensitive
- multiline
- dotall
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a57ea778-009b-4b8e-94d0-e440c6ca235d)

10. Regex Extract, and input is
- string
- regex_pattern
- mode, with options are ["First Match", "All Matches", "First Group", "All Groups"]
- case_insensitive
- multiline
- dotall
- group_index
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4d1fce8-f2a9-422d-8b62-9ac90d50060a)

intent_extractor.intent_summary: Add 10 new string manipulation nodes to the ComfyUI framework: StringConcatenate, StringSubstring, StringLength, CaseConverter, StringTrim, StringReplace, StringContains, StringCompare, RegexMatch, and RegexExtract. These nodes implement basic string operations as requested in an RFC, with various input parameters for string manipulation, case conversion, trimming, replacement, containment checks, comparisons, and regex operations.
intent_extractor.non_goals: No explicit non-goals stated. The PR focuses on implementing the 10 specified string nodes without mentioning additional features or scope beyond the RFC requirements.

explorer_run.last_summary: Bootstrap exploration complete. Reviewed new string manipulation nodes in comfy_extras/nodes_string.py and registration in nodes.py. All 10 nodes implement basic string operations with required inputs and return types. Key observations: StringSubstring lacks bounds checking which could cause silent empty results; CaseConverter and StringTrim have fallback branches returning input unchanged; RegexExtract handles multiple modes with proper error catching. No critical defects found in diff context,

A dedicated structured extraction task is added for regex-specific tuple handling. This balances comprehensiveness with clear boundaries.

sections.content:
Declared input contracts (upstream): Assume runtime inputs satisfy the framework's declared input schema for each entry point (e.g. plugin/node INPUT_TYPES, public API parameter types, protobuf/JSON schema required fields, OpenAPI required properties). Do not report missing null/None/empty guards for parameters that are required and non-optional in that schema. Treat absent null checks as a defect only when the input is explicitly optional (Optional, nullable, ANY/wildcard, or documented as accepting missing/absent values), or when the diff itself introduces nullable handling that implies such values can arrive.
In-function contracts (downstream of schema): Declared input schemas do not prove branch exhaustiveness or return-type correctness inside the handler. Missing else/return, implicit None when RETURN_TYPES or annotations promise a concrete type, wrong element from structured returns (regex tuples, ORM rows, JSON nodes), and None in aggregations (join, serializers) are in scope even when enums or COMBO lists document allowed values. Do not dismiss those solely because a UI or schema restricts inputs—use needs_verification only when the failure mode depends on undocumented runtime bypass (manual edits, schema drift). This rule does NOT override the upstream declared-input rule: do not report missing None/null guards on required, non-optional parameters solely because runtime might violate types.

Declared input contracts (upstream): Assume runtime inputs satisfy the framework's declared input schema for each entry point (e.g. plugin/node INPUT_TYPES, public API parameter types, protobuf/JSON schema required fields, OpenAPI required properties). Do not report missing null/None/empty guards for parameters that are required and non-optional in that schema. Treat absent null checks as a defect only when the input is explicitly optional (Optional, nullable, ANY/wildcard, or documented as accepting missing/absent values), or when the diff itself introduces nullable handling that implies such values can arrive.
In-function contracts (downstream of schema): Declared input schemas do not prove branch exhaustiveness or return-type correctness inside the handler. Missing else/return, implicit None when RETURN_TYPES or annotations promise a concrete type, wrong element from structured returns (regex tuples, ORM rows, JSON nodes), and None in aggregations (join, serializers) are in scope even when enums or COMBO lists document allowed values. Do not dismiss those solely because a UI or schema restricts inputs—use needs_verification only when the failure mode depends on undocumented runtime bypass (manual edits, schema drift). This rule does NOT override the upstream declared-input rule: do not report missing None/null guards on required, non-optional parameters solely because runtime might violate types.
